children: Consumer confidence in Germany dropped unexpectedly sharply, dragged down by rising energy prices as tensions escalated in the Middle East.

Germany's consumer-climate index, published Friday by the Nuremberg Institute for Market Decisions and GfK, fell to minus 30.6 in its forecast for October, its lowest level since May, from minus 26.8 in September. Economists polled last week by The Wall Street Journal expected a smaller decline to minus 27.2.

"The majority of households expect high energy prices to reduce their purchasing power," said Rolf Buerkl, head of the survey at NIM. "As a result, they are more skeptical about their income expectations for the next twelve months."

Expectations for personal incomes declined to their lowest since April, shortly before a temporary tax rebate for fuel introduced by the German government in the aftermath of the start of the war in Iran. The survey also showed an increase in households' willingness to save.

Oil prices spiked earlier this month after renewed U.S. strikes on Iran. Higher energy prices across the eurozone in recent months were among the reasons that prompted the European Central Bank to raise its key interest rate.
German consumer sentiment has been sharply negative since 2022, shortly after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine that sent energy prices upward, hitting households and businesses.

The decline in confidence comes despite the Ifo Institute's business sentiment index on Thursday rising to a more-than-three-year high. A leading group of German economists on Thursday also nearly doubled their growth forecasts for this year compared with their March projections.

"German consumers don't share the resilience story other leading indicators have been telling us lately," said Carsten Brzeski, economist at ING. "At least someone is reacting to surging energy prices and interest rates."
Meanwhile, consumer sentiment in the U.K. edged higher as perceptions of personal finances and the economy improved, data also published Friday showed.
